title: Marcus Aurelius: The Emperor Who Wrote to Himself | Biography for Sleep
description:
Fall asleep to the true story of Marcus Aurelius, the Roman emperor who wrote the Meditations. In this calm, slow biography we follow him from a quiet childhood on the Caelian Hill in Rome in 121 AD, through his teachers, his letters to Fronto, his marriage to Faustina and the peaceful years beside Antoninus Pius, to two decades on the throne: floods, plague, the long winters by the Danube where he wrote his private notebook by lamplight, the burned letters of a rebel, Athens, and his last days in 180 AD. About 143 minutes of gentle narration over a quiet fireside sound.

23:18 3. A Sudden Heir

📚 SOURCES
- Marcus Aurelius, Meditations, translated by George Long (1862, public domain; text from Standard Ebooks)
- Letters of Marcus Aurelius and Fronto (letter on a day at the grape harvest, Ad M. Caes. 4.6; romanletters.org)
- Cassius Dio, Roman History, books 71-72 (Avidius Cassius, the burned letters, Athens, "a kingdom of gold")
- Historia Augusta, Life of Marcus Aurelius and Life of Antoninus Pius (a later and less reliable source; stories from it are marked as later accounts in the narration)
- Encyclopaedia Britannica: Marcus Aurelius; Antoninus Pius; Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy: Marcus Aurelius
- Livius.org: Marcus Aurelius

title: Jane Austen: A Quiet Life of Ink and Wit | Biography for Sleep
description:
Fall asleep to the true story of Jane Austen, the clergyman's daughter who wrote Pride and Prejudice, Emma and Persuasion at a small table in a Hampshire cottage. In this calm, slow biography we follow her from a snowy winter birth at Steventon rectory in 1775, through the family plays in the barn, her teenage notebooks, country dances and Tom Lefroy, a first novel turned down unread, the years in Bath and Southampton with her sailor brothers, the quiet home at Chawton where her books finally went out into the world "By a Lady", a visit to the Prince Regent's library, and her last days in Winchester in 1817. About 138 minutes of gentle narration over a quiet fireside sound.

- Henry Austen, Biographical Notice of the Author (1817, in Northanger Abbey and Persuasion)
- James Edward Austen-Leigh, A Memoir of Jane Austen (1870)

Short lines are quoted only from Jane Austen's own letters and novels and from family letters of the time (all public domain). Stories that come only from later family memory (for example the fainting at the news of the move to Bath, the creaking door at Chawton, the young man met at the seaside) are marked as such in the narration. Nobody knows for certain what illness she died of; the narration says so.

title: Charles Dickens and the Story of A Christmas Carol | Biography for Sleep
description:
Fall asleep to the true story of Charles Dickens, the boy from the blacking warehouse who grew up to write Oliver Twist, David Copperfield, Great Expectations and, in one cold autumn, A Christmas Carol. In this calm, slow biography we follow him from a winter birth in Portsmouth in 1812, through golden childhood years by the Medway, a hard year tying up pots of boot blacking while his father sat in the Marshalsea debtors' prison, shorthand and the reporters' gallery, the first sketch dropped into a dark letter-box, the sudden fame of Mr. Pickwick, a stormy crossing to America, and the six weeks of night walks in which he wrote A Christmas Carol. Then the busy middle years, the real shadows of his marriage, the public readings, Gad's Hill, and a summer evening in 1870. About 147 minutes of gentle narration over a quiet fireside sound.

Short lines are quoted only from Dickens's own public-domain writing (A Christmas Carol, his prefaces, essays and letters) and from Thackeray's 1844 review. Stories that come from later memory or later accounts (the walks to Gad's Hill with his father, the New York crowds asking about Little Nell, the girl who asked whether Father Christmas would die too) are marked as such in the narration. Dates of the blacking-warehouse year are uncertain, and the narration says so.
